questions.questionText: Define nuclear family.
questions.explanation: A family made up of parents (mother and father) and their biological or adopted children living together [1 mark].

questions.questionText: State one characteristic of a polygamous family.
questions.explanation: A husband is legally or customarily married to more than one wife at the same time [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Name another family type.
questions.explanation: Extended family / single-parent family / child-headed family / blended family [1 mark].

questions.questionText: State one role of parents.
questions.explanation: Providing basic needs (food, shelter, clothing, education), moral guidance, love, and protection [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Give one example of family wealth.
questions.explanation: Livestock (cattle/goats), land/property, savings, or farming tools/equipment [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Define genealogy.
questions.explanation: A record or family tree showing lineage, ancestors, and relationships across generations [1 mark].

questions.questionText: State one reason for preserving genealogy.
questions.explanation: Helps individuals know their roots/identity, inheritance rights, and prevents marriage between close relatives [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Define totem.
questions.explanation: A sacred animal, object, or symbol (mutupo/isibongo) that identifies a clan or lineage [1 mark].

questions.questionText: State one reason for respecting a totem.
questions.explanation: Shows sympathy, care, and respect for someone else's feelings by putting yourself in their situation [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Name one indigenous grain-processing tool.
questions.explanation: Acknowledging ancestors (kurova guva / umbuyiso), rainmaking ceremonies (mukwerera), or observing chisi [1 mark].

questions.questionText: State one use of a mortar and pestle.
questions.explanation: Grinding or pounding grain (maize, sorghum, millet, groundnuts) into meal or paste [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Name one indigenous staple food.
questions.explanation: Sadza (maize meal) / mapfunde (sorghum) / zviyo (finger millet) / nyimo (bambara nuts) [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Define heritage site.
questions.explanation: A place or monument of historical, cultural, or natural significance preserved for future generations [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Name one Zimbabwean heritage site.
questions.explanation: Great Zimbabwe / Matobo Hills / Victoria Falls (Mosi-oa-Tunya) / Khami Ruins / Mana Pools [1 mark].

questions.questionText: State one way to protect a heritage site.
questions.explanation: Enforcing anti-vandalism laws, fencing/guarding the site, educating visitors, and avoiding litter/graffiti [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Name one traditional leader.
questions.explanation: Chief (Mambo/Nkosi), Headman (Sadunhu), or Village Head (Sabhuku) [1 mark].

questions.questionText: State one role of a traditional leader.
questions.explanation: Resolving local disputes, safeguarding cultural heritage/customs, and conserving local natural resources [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Define citizenship.
questions.explanation: Legal membership of a country carrying both constitutional rights and civic responsibilities [1 mark].

questions.questionText: State one citizen responsibility.
questions.explanation: Obeying national laws, paying taxes, protecting public property, or voting responsibly [1 mark].

questions.questionText: State the general voting age in Zimbabwe.
questions.explanation: 18 years old and above [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Name one national symbol.
questions.explanation: National Flag / Zimbabwe Bird / National Anthem / Coat of Arms [1 mark].

questions.questionText: State one purpose of a national symbol.
questions.explanation: Unites citizens, represents national sovereignty and pride, and commemorates Zimbabwe's liberation heritage [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Define democracy.
questions.explanation: A system of government where power rests with the people who elect leaders freely and fairly [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Name the national law-making institution.
questions.explanation: Parliament of Zimbabwe (National Assembly and Senate) [1 mark].

questions.questionText: State one reason for a secret ballot.
questions.explanation: Protects voters' privacy so they can choose freely without intimidation or bribery [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Define gender equality.
questions.explanation: Equal rights, responsibilities, and opportunities for females and males in all areas of life [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Give one example of gender equality at home.
questions.explanation: Sharing household chores, cooking, cleaning, and educational support fairly between boys and girls [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Define production.
questions.explanation: Creating or making goods and services to satisfy human needs and wants [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Define consumption.
questions.explanation: Using goods and services to satisfy human needs and wants [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Define distribution.
questions.explanation: Moving goods and services from producers to consumers (transport, wholesaling, retailing) [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Define entrepreneur.
questions.explanation: A person who identifies an opportunity, organises resources, and takes calculated risk to start a business [1 mark].

questions.questionText: State one benefit of entrepreneurship.
questions.explanation: Creates jobs, increases community income, supplies useful goods/services, and boosts economic growth [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Define scarcity.
questions.explanation: The basic economic condition where human wants exceed limited available resources [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Define budget.
questions.explanation: A financial plan estimating expected income and planned expenditure over a specific period [1 mark].

questions.questionText: State one benefit of saving.
questions.explanation: Provides emergency funds, finances education or business goals, and avoids unnecessary debt [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Define opportunity cost.
questions.explanation: The value of the next best alternative given up when making a choice [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Define rural-urban migration.
questions.explanation: Movement of people from countryside villages to towns and cities to live or work [1 mark].

questions.questionText: State one cause of rural-urban migration.
questions.explanation: Seeking formal employment, better schools/hospitals, or fleeing rural drought [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Define population density.
questions.explanation: The average number of people living per unit area (e.g., people per square kilometre) [1 mark].

questions.questionText: What is a census?
questions.explanation: An official count and survey of a country's entire population carried out periodically (every 10 years in Zimbabwe) [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Define pollution.
questions.explanation: Contamination of air, water, or land by harmful substances or waste [1 mark].

questions.questionText: State one effect of deforestation.
questions.explanation: Soil erosion, loss of wildlife habitat, reduced rainfall infiltration, and fuelwood shortages [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Give one way to conserve water.
questions.explanation: Fixing leaking taps, harvesting rainwater, mulching gardens, and reusing greywater [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Define sustainable development.
questions.explanation: Meeting present needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Define self-awareness.
questions.explanation: Understanding your own emotions, strengths, weaknesses, values, and behaviour [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Define peer pressure.
questions.explanation: Social influence from people of the same age group encouraging someone to copy their choices [1 mark].

questions.questionText: State one way to resist harmful peer pressure.
questions.explanation: Say "No" firmly, leave risky situations, choose positive friends, and seek guidance from trusted adults [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Name one hygiene practice.
questions.explanation: Washing hands with soap, bathing daily, brushing teeth, and wearing clean clothes [1 mark].

questions.questionText: State one action when abuse is suspected.
questions.explanation: Report immediately to a trusted parent/teacher, Victim Friendly Unit (police), or Childline (116) [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Give one safe leisure activity.
questions.explanation: Playing football/netball, reading, gardening, chess, choir/traditional dance [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Name one reliable health-information source.
questions.explanation: Clinics/hospitals, qualified doctors/nurses, Ministry of Health guidance, or approved school textbooks [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Define volunteerism.
questions.explanation: Freely offering time and skills to help others or improve the community without expecting pay [1 mark].

questions.questionText: State one benefit of volunteerism.
questions.explanation: Strengthens community unity, builds practical teamwork skills, and helps vulnerable neighbours [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Define corporate social responsibility.
questions.explanation: A business's voluntary commitment to act ethically and support social and environmental wellbeing [1 mark].

questions.questionText: State one ICT method of preserving heritage.
questions.explanation: Recording elders' oral histories on audio/video, photographing artefacts, or building digital museum archives [1 mark].

questions.questionText: State one risk of careless online sharing.
questions.explanation: Cyberbullying, identity theft, scamming, stalking, or permanent damage to reputation [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Define religious tolerance.
questions.explanation: Respecting and accepting people's right to hold and practise different religious beliefs peacefully [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Name one Christian festival.
questions.explanation: Christmas / Easter / Good Friday / Ascension Day [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Name one Pillar of Islam.
questions.explanation: Shahadah (faith), Salah (prayer), Zakat (charity), Sawm (fasting in Ramadan), or Hajj (pilgrimage) [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Name one sacred text associated with Judaism.
questions.explanation: The Torah / Tanakh (Hebrew Bible) / Talmud [1 mark].

questions.questionText: A learner finds an old cultural artefact at school. What should happen next?
questions.explanation: Leave it undisturbed if fragile, report to the teacher/head/National Museums & Monuments of Zimbabwe so it is safely documented and preserved [2 marks].

questions.questionText: A family must choose between repairing a leaking roof and buying a luxury item. Which should come first?
questions.explanation: Repairing the leaking roof must come first because shelter is a basic need protecting health and property, whereas a luxury item is a want [2 marks].

questions.questionText: Residents work together to repair a damaged community water point. What is this an example of?
questions.explanation: Community cooperation / self-help / volunteerism (nhimbe/ilima spirit) [2 marks].

questions.questionText: A company supports a school and improves waste management near its operations. What principle is shown?
questions.explanation: Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) and environmental stewardship [2 marks].

questions.questionText: A learner receives a threatening message online. What is a safe response?
questions.explanation: Do not reply, save/screenshot evidence, block the sender, and report immediately to a parent, teacher, or school head [2 marks].

questions.questionText: Two neighbours have different religions. What promotes peaceful coexistence?
questions.explanation: Religious tolerance, mutual respect, dialogue, and participating together in shared community work [2 marks].

questions.questionText: A school gives boys and girls equal leadership opportunities. What value is promoted?
questions.explanation: Gender equality and fairness (non-discrimination) [2 marks].

questions.questionText: A village experiences prolonged low rainfall and crop failure. What hazard is described?
questions.explanation: Drought (climatic natural hazard) [2 marks].

questions.questionText: A town receives many new residents from rural areas. What process is occurring?
questions.explanation: Rural-urban migration / rapid urbanisation [2 marks].

questions.questionText: A school records elders’ oral histories and stores them digitally with permission. What is being done?
questions.explanation: Digital preservation of indigenous oral heritage and cultural knowledge [2 marks].

questions.questionText: A consumer finds a product is faulty. What should the consumer keep?
questions.explanation: Keep the purchase receipt/proof of payment and warranty card so the item can be exchanged, repaired, or refunded [2 marks].

questions.questionText: A farmer receives a heavy-rain forecast. How can this help?
questions.explanation: Helps the farmer delay chemical spraying, clear drainage channels, protect harvested crops, and time planting safely [2 marks].

questions.questionText: A wetland provides water and animal habitat. What should the community do?
questions.explanation: Conserve the wetland by preventing dumping, farming, or building inside it, and following EMA conservation rules [2 marks].

questions.questionText: A learner is pressured to misuse a harmful substance. What is safest?
questions.explanation: Say "No" assertively, walk away immediately, avoid peers who pressure substance abuse, and inform a trusted adult [2 marks].

questions.questionText: A community wants tourism income without damaging a heritage site. What should it do?
questions.explanation: Practise sustainable/ecotourism: use trained local guides, restrict visitor numbers/paths, ban littering, and reinvest fees in conservation [2 marks].

questions.questionText: A school wants to reduce litter. Which approach is most suitable?
questions.explanation: Place labelled bins (reduce/reuse/recycle), run learner clean-up duty rosters, and educate the school against littering [2 marks].

questions.questionText: A family wants to save for school expenses. What is a sensible first step?
questions.explanation: Draw up a family budget separating essential needs from wants, cut unnecessary spending, and set aside regular savings [2 marks].

questions.questionText: A class elects a representative. What makes the election fair?
questions.explanation: Equal voting rights for all eligible learners, secret ballot voting, neutral counting, and acceptance of results [2 marks].

questions.questionText: Two families disagree about a shared resource. What should they do first?
questions.explanation: Hold a calm, respectful dialogue (mediated by an elder or community leader if needed) to agree on a fair sharing schedule [2 marks].

questions.questionText: A learner hears an unverified health rumour. What is responsible?
questions.explanation: Do not spread the rumour; verify the facts from a qualified clinic nurse/doctor or Ministry of Health official [2 marks].

questions.questionText: A school garden uses rainwater and compost. What does this demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Sustainable resource management (water harvesting and organic waste recycling) [2 marks].

questions.questionText: A map contains symbols for a clinic, river and road. What explains the symbols?
questions.explanation: The map key (legend) explains what every symbol and colour represents [2 marks].

questions.questionText: A family has limited income. Which should be prioritised?
questions.explanation: Basic needs first: nutritious food, clean water, healthcare, shelter, and school fees before non-essential wants [2 marks].

questions.questionText: A youth group organises a supervised sports day. What is important?
questions.explanation: Adult supervision, first-aid kit readiness, safe cleared playing surfaces, and fair inclusive rules for all youth [2 marks].

questions.questionText: A learner experiences abuse. What is a safe action?
questions.explanation: Speak out immediately to a trusted teacher, guardian, school counsellor, Victim Friendly Unit, or Childline 116 [2 marks].

questions.questionText: A youth group teaches forgiveness after conflict. What value is promoted?
questions.explanation: Reconciliation, empathy, tolerance, and peaceful conflict resolution [2 marks].

questions.questionText: An entrepreneur researches customers and costs before starting a business. What is shown?
questions.explanation: Market research, business planning, and financial risk assessment [2 marks].

questions.questionText: A village protects vegetation along a stream. What benefit can result?
questions.explanation: Reduces stream-bank soil erosion, prevents siltation, keeps water cleaner, and protects riparian wildlife habitats [2 marks].

questions.questionText: A family shares household tasks fairly. What is promoted?
questions.explanation: Gender equality, cooperation, mutual respect, and shared family responsibility [2 marks].

questions.questionText: A community cleans a public facility without payment. What is this?
questions.explanation: Volunteerism / civic responsibility / community service [2 marks].

questions.questionText: Discuss five ways families can promote strong relationships.
questions.explanation: 1. Honest open communication. 2. Spending quality time together. 3. Fair sharing of chores and mutual respect. 4. Supporting each other in illness or crisis. 5. Forgiving mistakes and resolving disagreements calmly [5 marks].

questions.questionText: Explain how family roles contribute to children’s wellbeing.
questions.explanation: Parents provide shelter, food, and school fees [2 marks]; guidance and discipline teach good Ubuntu/Unhu morals [2 marks]; extended family offers emotional warmth and safety [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Discuss why family genealogies and oral histories should be preserved.
questions.explanation: Preserves family history and cultural identity [2 marks]; clarifies kinship/totem ties to prevent taboo marriages [2 marks]; guides family inheritance and elders' wisdom [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Explain the importance of totems in Zimbabwean identity.
questions.explanation: Totems (mitupo/izibongo) connect people to clans and ancestors [2 marks], promote social solidarity across communities [1 mark], regulate marriage customs [1 mark], and encourage conservation by protecting totem animals [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Discuss how Indigenous Religion can promote moral behaviour and unity.
questions.explanation: Teaches Unhu/Ubuntu (honesty, respect for elders, hospitality) [2 marks], reinforces community unity through shared ceremonies like nhimbe/mukwerera [2 marks], and deters crime through reverence for ancestors [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Explain how religious tolerance promotes peace.
questions.explanation: Prevents religious discrimination and violent conflict [2 marks], fosters dialogue and cooperation on shared community projects [2 marks], and protects constitutional freedom of worship [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Describe how religions can encourage positive moral values.
questions.explanation: All major religions teach honesty, compassion for the poor/sick, truthfulness, forgiveness, respect for life, and obeying just laws [5 marks].

questions.questionText: Explain the importance of heritage sites to Zimbabwe.
questions.explanation: Heritage sites preserve national history and identity (e.g., Great Zimbabwe) [2 marks], generate tourism jobs and foreign currency [2 marks], and serve as outdoor educational research centres [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Discuss practical measures for conserving heritage sites.
questions.explanation: Enforce National Museums & Monuments laws against vandalism [2 marks], fence and guard sites [1 mark], control visitor erosion [1 mark], and run school/community heritage education [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Explain the roles of traditional leaders in communities.
questions.explanation: Chiefs, headmen, and village heads settle customary disputes peacefully [2 marks], safeguard traditional culture and ceremonies [1 mark], allocate communal land fairly, and mobilise environmental conservation [2 marks].

questions.questionText: Discuss responsible participation in a democracy.
questions.explanation: Registering and voting peacefully in elections [2 marks], obeying the Constitution and laws [1 mark], attending community consultations, and holding leaders accountable peacefully [2 marks].

questions.questionText: Explain the importance of national symbols.
questions.explanation: National symbols (Flag, Anthem, Zimbabwe Bird, Coat of Arms) inspire unity across regions [2 marks], honour independence heroes [2 marks], and identify Zimbabwe internationally [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Discuss why laws are important in society.
questions.explanation: Protect citizens' fundamental rights and safety [2 marks], resolve disputes fairly in courts [2 marks], prevent anarchy/crime, and ensure equal treatment for all [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Explain why elections should be fair and secret.
questions.explanation: Secret ballots prevent voter intimidation and vote-buying [2 marks]; fair transparent elections ensure chosen leaders hold genuine public legitimacy and peaceful transfer of power [3 marks].

questions.questionText: Discuss the importance of gender equality.
questions.explanation: Unlocks full economic potential by educating both girls and boys [2 marks], ensures equal pay and leadership representation [2 marks], and reduces poverty and gender-based violence [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Explain how production, distribution and consumption are connected.
questions.explanation: Producers manufacture raw or finished goods [2 marks], distributors transport and retail them to markets [2 marks], and consumers buy/use them—creating demand that drives further production [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Discuss how entrepreneurship can create employment.
questions.explanation: Entrepreneurs start workshops, farms, shops, or tech firms [2 marks] that hire local workers directly [2 marks] and stimulate demand for local suppliers and transporters [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Explain why budgeting and saving matter.
questions.explanation: Budgeting tracks income vs expenses so needs come before wants [2 marks], prevents overspending/debt [1 mark], and builds savings for school fees, emergencies, and investments [2 marks].

questions.questionText: Discuss how scarcity affects family choices.
questions.explanation: Because household money and time are limited while needs/wants are unlimited [2 marks], families must prioritise essentials (food, health, education) [2 marks] and postpone luxuries [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Explain opportunity cost using a realistic example.
questions.explanation: Opportunity cost is the next best alternative forgone when choosing [2 marks]. Example: Spending $50 on school books instead of new trainers means the trainers are the opportunity cost [3 marks].

questions.questionText: Discuss causes and effects of rural-urban migration.
questions.explanation: Causes (push/pull): Rural unemployment/drought vs urban jobs, colleges, and clinics [3 marks]. Effects: Urban overcrowding/unemployment vs labour shortage in villages and remittance income [2 marks].

questions.questionText: Explain pressures created by rapid urbanisation.
questions.explanation: Housing shortages and informal settlements [1 mark], strain on clean water, sewage, electricity, clinics, and schools [2 marks], traffic congestion, and higher urban unemployment/crime [2 marks].

questions.questionText: Discuss ways to conserve natural resources.
questions.explanation: Contour farming and afforestation protect soil and forests [2 marks], rainwater harvesting/fixing leaks saves water [1 mark], anti-poaching protects wildlife [1 mark], and recycling reduces mining/waste [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Explain effects of deforestation on people and the environment.
questions.explanation: Causes severe soil erosion and siltation of dams [2 marks], destroys animal habitats and medicinal trees [2 marks], increases flooding and fuelwood scarcity [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Discuss ways schools can reduce pollution and waste.
questions.explanation: Provide sorted litter/recycling bins [2 marks], compost organic garden/kitchen waste [1 mark], reuse paper/containers, and educate clubs on zero-littering [2 marks].

questions.questionText: Explain sustainable development using Zimbabwean examples.
questions.explanation: Using resources to meet today's needs without ruining them for future generations [2 marks]. Examples: CAMPFIRE wildlife conservation, solar micro-grids, and Pfumvudza conservation farming [3 marks].

questions.questionText: Discuss preparation for droughts and floods.
questions.explanation: Droughts: Plant drought-tolerant small grains (sorghum/millet), harvest water, and store grain reserves [3 marks]. Floods: Avoid building on floodplains, clear storm drains, and follow CPU evacuation alerts [2 marks].

questions.questionText: Explain how weather information helps farmers.
questions.explanation: Seasonal rainfall forecasts guide planting dates and seed varieties [2 marks], storm/frost warnings protect livestock and harvested grain [2 marks], and drought alerts aid irrigation planning [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Discuss positive and negative effects of tourism.
questions.explanation: Positive: Earns foreign currency, creates jobs/craft markets, and funds conservation [3 marks]. Negative: Littering, cultural erosion, wildlife disturbance, or price inflation [2 marks].

questions.questionText: Explain why occupational safety matters.
questions.explanation: Prevents workplace injuries/deaths (e.g., mines, farms, workshops) [2 marks], requires PPE (helmets, gloves, goggles) and training [2 marks], and protects family livelihoods from lost income [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Discuss the value of volunteerism.
questions.explanation: Improves public spaces (cleanups, mentoring, caring for the elderly) without pay [2 marks], builds empathy and leadership skills [2 marks], and unites neighbours [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Explain how corporate social responsibility benefits communities.
questions.explanation: Companies fund school classrooms/scholarships, clinics, boreholes, and environmental clean-ups [3 marks], improving living standards while earning community trust [2 marks].

questions.questionText: Discuss how ICT supports education and heritage.
questions.explanation: ICT provides e-learning libraries, online lessons, and typed research for learners [3 marks], while digital photography, audio recordings, and archives preserve elders' languages and monuments [2 marks].

questions.questionText: Explain risks of irresponsible social-media use and how learners can stay safe.
questions.explanation: Risks: Cyberbullying, predators, scams, addiction, and privacy leaks [2 marks]. Safety: Keep accounts private, never share personal locations/photos with strangers, block bullies, and tell a trusted adult [3 marks].

questions.questionText: Discuss causes and effects of negative peer pressure.
questions.explanation: Causes: Desire to fit in, low self-esteem, lack of adult guidance [2 marks]. Effects: Drug/substance abuse, truancy, risky behaviour, and falling grades [3 marks].

questions.questionText: Explain healthy ways adolescents can manage stress and change.
questions.explanation: Talk openly with parents, teachers, or counsellors [2 marks], join positive sports/clubs [1 mark], get enough sleep and exercise, and avoid alcohol/drugs [2 marks].

questions.questionText: Discuss personal hygiene and healthy lifestyles.
questions.explanation: Daily bathing, handwashing before food/after toilets, brushing teeth, balanced meals, regular exercise, and clean drinking water prevent infectious and lifestyle diseases [5 marks].

questions.questionText: Explain how communities can protect children from abuse.
questions.explanation: Educate children on safe vs unsafe touches and reporting rights [2 marks], maintain watchful community care, and promptly report suspected abuse to Police Victim Friendly Unit or Childline 116 [3 marks].

questions.questionText: Discuss the importance of reliable health information.
questions.explanation: Verified advice from clinics, doctors, and Ministry of Health prevents dangerous myths, encourages timely vaccination and clean sanitation, and saves lives during outbreaks like cholera [5 marks].

questions.questionText: Explain how conflict-resolution skills strengthen communities.
questions.explanation: Active listening, mediation, forgiveness, and fair compromise solve disputes without violence [3 marks], maintaining neighbourhood trust and teamwork for community development [2 marks].
